about: Three real questions asked in Caltech CS 156 (the moderator relays the online audience in the Q&A at the end of Lectures 14 and 15). Text copied from the caption chunks of the knowledge-graph pilot (CC BY video licence field). Each question's own Q&A passages hold the professor's answer, so they are excluded from retrieval for that question (leakage rule: derived_from). The reference points are our reading of the professor's answer (one rater).

questions.question: What happens when the points are not linearly separable?

reference.point: If the data are badly non-separable, apply a nonlinear transformation (go to a Z space).
If they are only slightly non-separable, use the soft-margin SVM, which allows a few margin errors and penalizes them.
In practice, both together: a nonlinear transformation plus the soft version.

questions.stratum: cross-concept (ours): the answer joins Lecture 14 (hard margin) with Lecture 15 (soft margin, kernels)

questions.question: Is it possible to combine kernels to produce new, different kernels?

reference.point: Yes, if the combination is legitimate: there must still be a Z space in which it is an inner product (a valid kernel).

questions.question: So is it safe to assume, then, that if you do the transformation to an infinite-dimensional space, the data will be linearly separable there?

reference.point: Safe but not certain: counter-examples can be built.
You do not need to know in advance: apply the machinery and check whether the points are classified correctly.
